description: PRD-50: Universal Orchestrator Router — Transform the orchestrator from a workflow-only executor into a universal request router that handles all incoming requests (Chatbot, Jira triggers, APIs) and intelligently routes them to the right pre-configured agent or recipe/workflow.

userStories.title: Create RequestEnvelope and RoutingDecision models
userStories.description: As a developer, I need standard data models for the universal request envelope and routing decision so that all channels produce consistent input and the router produces consistent output.
acceptanceCriteria: Create orchestrator/core/models/routing.py with all models

RequestEnvelope Pydantic model with fields: id (UUID), source (ChannelSource), content (str), raw_payload (Dict), user (RequestUser), workspace_id (UUID), metadata (Dict), override_agent_id (Optional[int]), override_workflow_id (Optional[int]), conversation_id (Optional[UUID]), timestamp (datetime)

RoutingDecision Pydantic model with fields: route_type (str: agent|workflow|orchestrate), agent_id (Optional[int]), workflow_id (Optional[int]), confidence (float), reasoning (str), cached (bool), intent_category (str)
ChannelSource enum with values: chatbot, jira_trigger, slack, whatsapp, api, workflow
RequestUser model with fields: id (Optional[str]), email (Optional[str]), name (Optional[str]), auth_type (str), clerk_user_id (Optional[str])

RoutingDecisionRecord SQLAlchemy ORM model for routing_decisions table with fields: id, request_id, envelope_hash, source, route_type, agent_id, workflow_id, confidence, cached, was_corrected, corrected_agent_id, created_at
RoutingRule SQLAlchemy ORM model for routing_rules table with fields: id, workspace_id, source_pattern, intent_keywords, target_agent_id, target_workflow_id, priority, is_active, created_at
UnroutedEvent SQLAlchemy ORM model for unrouted_events table with fields: id, workspace_id, source, content, raw_payload, reason, created_at
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Build routing cache with TTL and workspace scoping
userStories.description: As the system, I need to cache routing decisions per workspace so repeated patterns resolve instantly without LLM calls.
acceptanceCriteria: Create orchestrator/core/routing/__init__.py (empty)
Create orchestrator/core/routing/cache.py with RoutingCache class
In-memory cache using dict keyed by (workspace_id, hash(normalized_content + source))
Cache TTL: 24 hours default, configurable via ROUTING_CACHE_TTL_HOURS env var
get(workspace_id, content, source) method — returns cached RoutingDecision or None
put(workspace_id, content, source, decision) method — stores decision with timestamp
record_correction(workspace_id, content, source, correct_agent_id) method — updates cached entry if same correction made 2+ times
clear(workspace_id) method — clear all cache for a workspace
stats() method — returns cache size, hit rate, top cached routes
Expired entries cleaned up on access (lazy eviction)
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Build routing engine — Tier 0 and Tier 2 (override and rules)
userStories.description: As the orchestrator, I need the core routing engine that handles user overrides (Tier 0) and rule-based matching (Tier 2) without LLM calls.
acceptanceCriteria: Create orchestrator/core/routing/engine.py with UniversalRouter class
Constructor takes db session and optional RoutingCache instance
async route(envelope: RequestEnvelope) -> RoutingDecision method
Tier 0: If envelope.override_agent_id set, return RoutingDecision with route_type='agent', confidence=1.0, reasoning='User override'
Tier 0: If envelope.override_workflow_id set, return RoutingDecision with route_type='workflow', confidence=1.0, reasoning='User override'
Tier 1: Check RoutingCache — if hit, return cached decision with cached=True
Tier 2: Query routing_rules table for matching workspace_id + source_pattern. If match, return decision.
Tier 2b: Query TriggerSubscription table if source is jira_trigger — if matching trigger has agent_id/workflow_id, use it
Tier 2c: Use existing IntentClassifier from core/services/intent_classifier.py for keyword-based matching
If no match at any tier, return None (caller handles LLM fallback)
Log every routing decision to routing_decisions table
Typecheck passes
userStories.notes: Tier 3 (LLM classification) added in next story

userStories.title: Add Tier 3 LLM classification to routing engine
userStories.description: As the orchestrator, I need LLM-based intent classification as a fallback when cache and rules don't match.
acceptanceCriteria: Add _classify_with_llm(envelope: RequestEnvelope) async method to UniversalRouter
Query database for all active agents in the workspace with their names, descriptions, and assigned app names
Build a lightweight prompt: 'Given this request: {content}. Route to the best agent from: {agent_list}. Return agent_id and confidence.'
Use workspace's configured LLM provider/model via existing LLM manager
Parse LLM response to extract agent_id and confidence score
If confidence < 0.5, return route_type='orchestrate' (full decomposition needed)
Cache the LLM result via RoutingCache.put() for future Tier 1 hits
Update route() method: after Tier 2 returns None, call _classify_with_llm()
If LLM also fails or returns low confidence, store in unrouted_events table
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Register routing API endpoints
userStories.description: As an admin, I need API endpoints to manage routing rules, view decisions, and record corrections.
acceptanceCriteria: Create orchestrator/api/routing.py with FastAPI router (prefix=/api/routing, tags=['Routing'])
GET /api/routing/decisions — list recent routing decisions with optional filters: source, agent_id, was_corrected. Paginated. Auth required via get_request_context_hybrid.
POST /api/routing/rules — create a routing rule: source_pattern (str), intent_keywords (List[str]), target_agent_id or target_workflow_id, priority (int). Auth required.
GET /api/routing/rules — list all active routing rules for the workspace. Auth required.
DELETE /api/routing/rules/{rule_id} — soft delete a routing rule. Auth required.
POST /api/routing/corrections — record user correction: request_id (UUID), correct_agent_id (int). Updates RoutingCache. Auth required.
GET /api/routing/cache/stats — return cache size, hit count, miss count, top 10 cached routes. Auth required.
Register router in orchestrator/main.py
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Build Jira Bug Triage workflow — Read and Analyze steps
userStories.description: As the system, I need the first half of the autonomous Bug Triage workflow: read the Jira ticket and analyze the codebase.
acceptanceCriteria: Create orchestrator/modules/workflows/recipes/jira_bug_triage.py
Define JiraBugTriageRecipe class with async execute(envelope: RequestEnvelope, db, workspace_id) method
Step 1 — Read Ticket: Use ComposioToolExecutor to call JIRA_GET_ISSUE with issue key from envelope.metadata
Step 2 — Analyze: Parse issue description, extract keywords, use CodeGraph search to find relevant files in the indexed codebase
Step 3 — Plan: Use LLM to generate a fix plan based on ticket description + relevant code snippets
Post the fix plan as a Jira comment via JIRA_ADD_COMMENT
Log progress at each step for observability
If any step fails, post failure summary as Jira comment and return error result
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Build Jira Bug Triage workflow — Fix, PR, and Update steps
userStories.description: As the system, I need the second half of the Bug Triage workflow: clone repo, apply fix, open PR, update Jira.
acceptanceCriteria: Extend JiraBugTriageRecipe with Steps 4-6
Step 4 — Clone & Fix: Use GITHUB_CREATE_BRANCH to create fix/{issue_key} branch, use GITHUB_CREATE_OR_UPDATE_FILE to apply code changes based on the plan
Step 5 — Open PR: Use GITHUB_CREATE_PULL_REQUEST with title referencing Jira ticket, description containing the fix plan
Step 6 — Update Jira: Use JIRA_UPDATE_ISSUE to transition ticket status. Add PR link as Jira comment via JIRA_ADD_COMMENT.
If any step fails, post failure summary as Jira comment and stop (no partial PRs)
Full workflow linked to TriggerSubscription so it can be dispatched by the router
Register recipe in a recipe registry so UniversalRouter can reference it by workflow_id
Typecheck passes
